title: Embed-cache-driven priority queue and adaptive soft-timeout for reranking endpoint
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The reranking endpoint is a frequent tail-latency hotspot when candidate sets include long contexts or heavy tokenized items. Current single-queue scheduling causes high p95/p99 latency and uneven token utilization across requests. We need an approach that improves p50/p95/p99 latency without regressing quality (NDCG/accuracy) and while preserving throughput for high-concurrency customers.

Goal: Implement a cache-aware priority queue plus adaptive soft-timeout policy that: (1) elevates requests with high embed-cache hit rates into a fast lane, (2) assigns token quotas per lane to avoid head-of-line blocking, and (3) gracefully degrades long requests with soft timeouts to return partial ranked lists rather than full stalls. Target: reduce p99 by 30% on rerank-heavy workloads and keep end-to-end NDCG drop <1% on customer eval sets.

Scope: changes limited to the reranker HTTP handler, scheduling layer, and KV/embed cache integration. No model changes. Includes metrics, dashboards, and a gradual rollout with canary and A/B analysis.

Why this design: Embedding lookups are frequently the cheapest portion; promoting embed-cache hits reduces expensive KV/model decoding cycles and yields high win rate for ranking latency. Soft timeouts allow returning useful partial results (e.g., top-k stable prefix) and avoid full request aborts while preserving downstream contract for clients that accept streaming/partial responses.

Out of scope: deep changes to model runtime kernel selection, persistent model quantization, or reshaping upstream retrieval algorithms beyond a thin priority hint.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for rerank endpoint reduced by >=30% on internal synthetic rerank workload
End-to-end NDCG on benchmark rerank set drops <1% (no statistical regression)
No increase in 95th percentile token cost per request beyond 5%
Feature gated and rolloutable with canary and A/B; ability to disable per-customer
Dashboards for lane-level latency, cache-hit ratio, token-quota exhaustion, and soft-timeout incidents are created
approach: Add a lightweight priority queue layer in front of the existing scheduler with 3 lanes: fast (embed-cache-hit), normal, slow (large-token requests)
Integrate embed cache signals: requests with >80% embed hit ratio are tagged fast; <20% tagged slow; others normal. Signal computed from prefetch stage (constant-time lookup)

Apply token leash per-lane: fast=high token quota small window, normal=medium quota, slow=conservative quota. Quotas enforced at the scheduler level to prevent a single slow request from blocking a lane

Introduce adaptive soft-timeout: per-request deadline derived from SLO and lane; on soft-timeout, return stable top-k prefix with explanation header and schedule background completion for non-blocking async post-processing
Speculative prefetch: for normal lane, opportunistically prefetch embeddings for next top-n candidates when slack in GPU queue is detected (limited to avoid cache thrash)
Metrics emitted: lane, embed_hit_ratio, tokens_charged, soft_timeout_fired, partial_response_ratio, final_score_variance
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind runtime gate and per-customer toggle
Stage 1 (internal): Enable for 10% internal traffic on synthetic rerank traffic (1 week)
Stage 2 (canary customers): Enable for 3 pilot customers with heavy rerank usage (2 weeks) and run A/B comparison against control
Stage 3 (gradual ramp): increase to 50% traffic if metrics stable; monitor p99, errors, and NDCG regressions
Stage 4: full rollout and cleanup of old scheduling codepaths (after 4 weeks of stability)
metrics: partial_response_incidents and percent of requests returned as partial
NDCG@10 and MAP on benchmark rerank sets
background-completion success rate and cleanup error rate
tests: Unit: scheduler lane assignment and token quota enforcement
Integration: end-to-end rerank flow with synthetic embed-cache hit/miss distributions
Perf: p99 tail run on k8s perf harness with 2000qps mixed candidate sizes
Regression: nightly eval comparing NDCG and latency against baseline job
Chaos: simulate cache flapping and slow model containers to validate soft-timeout semantics

2026-01-28 Design review (Aisha Patel): UX for partial results accepted. We will use stable top-k prefix plus provenance metadata. Design doc updated with sequence diagrams.

2026-01-30 Eng sync (Ravi): Prototype PR opened; initial perf numbers look promising on small scale. Blocking: need better per-request embed cache telemetry (ENG-31245) and a small change to the scheduler API (ENG-12011).
